items.q: Why must payment only go through the platform?
items.a: The warranty is tied to payment. If payment goes through the platform, we replace the lawyer and escalate when they don't respond or abandon the case. If paid outside, LexGo takes on no warranty obligation.

items.q: When do I see the lawyer's contact?
items.a: The communication channel opens once the lawyer confirms your order and you pay 10% of the service fee. Before that, neither side sees the other's contacts.

items.q: How do I extend the subscription to my family?
items.a: Once subscribed, you add the details of the family members covered by your plan to your profile. On Standard — your spouse; on Premium — your parents, spouse and dependent children.

items.q: Does the lawyer set the price themselves?
items.a: The price is formed by open criteria: region, experience and rating. A regional TOP-3 lawyer can raise the price up to 30%, a lawyer with 10+ years in a narrow area up to 20% — the reason is shown to you. A lawyer may also lower the price.

criminal.text:
This is a criminal-procedure matter, so every day counts.

1. Don't go to questioning without a lawyer — that's your right.
2. Every explanation you give can later be used as evidence.
3. If a restraint measure is chosen, it must be appealed within a short deadline — don't miss it.

The "full participation in the preliminary investigation" package suits you.

administrative.text:
This falls under administrative offences.

1. Request an official copy of the protocol and any video recording.
2. The objection deadline is short — count from today.
3. If a damage claim is filed alongside the fine, they are considered separately.

First have the document checked: often a formal defect in the protocol is grounds to void the case.
administrative.meta: Objection deadlines are calculated by the system

labor.text:
This is a labor dispute — usually resolved before court.

1. Gather the employment contract, the order and payment documents.
2. Send a written pre-claim to the employer and set a response deadline.
3. If there's no reply, a claim for reinstatement or unpaid wages is filed.

In labor disputes the claim deadline is short, so don't delay.
labor.meta: Labor Code · calculation of unpaid wages and compensation

civil.text:
This is a civil-law dispute.

1. Gather documents proving your right: contract, receipt, certificate.
2. Send a written pre-trial settlement proposal — it works in your favor later.
3. If there's no settlement, a claim is prepared; the state fee is based on the claim amount.

The "claim + representation in court" package suits you.
civil.meta: Claim deadline and state fee calculated automatically

economic.text:
This is a commercial (economic) dispute.

1. Keep the contract clauses and correspondence — an email is evidence too.
2. Even if no penalty is stated, you keep the right to claim for breach of obligation.
3. Order: pre-claim letter → calculation annex → claim to the economic court.

If we check the contract first, you'll see which clauses work against you.

corporate.text:
This is a corporate document matter — not a dispute, so it's resolved quickly.

1. Choose the activity type and tax regime in advance; changing later is costly.
2. Better to have the charter written individually, not from a template: shares, exit rules and management are decided there.
3. The trademark is registered separately from the company.

The "company registration + individual charter" package suits you.
corporate.meta: Registration and patenting deadlines are shown separately

generic.text:
I understand the matter, but to pin down the exact direction I need one or two details.

1. What happened and when?
2. Who is the other side — an individual, a company or a government body?
3. What documents do you have?

Write these and I'll name both the service type and a matching lawyer.
